::: {#sol-center-images}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
mean_image = images.float().mean(dim=0)
centered = images.float() - mean_image
largest_mean = centered.mean(dim=0).abs().max().item()
print(images.shape, mean_image.shape, centered.shape)
print(largest_mean)
```

`mean_image` has [shape](#def-shape) (8, 8),
and `images` has shape (`r py$n_images`, 8, 8),
yet PyTorch subtracts one from the other.
It uses the one average image for every image,
as if `mean_image` had been copied `r py$n_images` times along a new first dimension,
without making the copies.
Each pixel of `centered` now averages to 0 over the images,
to within `r format(py$largest_mean, digits = 2)`, a floating-point rounding error.

:::
